entries.title: II Samuel 15:1
segments: Men of weak minds and depraved hearts are peculiarly fond of personal decoration and external display, while the truly worthy and noble seek principally internal excellence and those spiritual ornaments which alone are, in the sight of the Lord, of great price.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:2
segments: The way of the gate; where the people assembled for judgment, or to obtain the king's decision of their cases.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:3
segments:
No man deputed of the king; he spoke as if David was negligent of his duty in not appointing him or some one to hear them. 
 
Familiarity and flattery, high promises of gratification, and strong expressions of regard for the people, mark the efforts of heartless demagogues to delude the multitude and promote their own elevation to office.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:5
segments: Many a good cause has been betrayed, and many a bad one promoted, by a kiss.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:6
segments: Stole the hearts; led the people to admire him.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:7
segments: Where godliness is respected, the most villanous conduct is sometimes masked under the semblance of piety, and those most pleased with the appearance of religion may be most readily deceived.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:9
segments: Go in peace; he probably hoped that Absalom was becoming better.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:11
segments: Called; invited to go with Absalom, supposing his object was, as he stated, a religious one.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:12
segments: Ahithophel; he had been a great friend to David, but now deserted him.
Giloh; in the mountainous parts of Judah.
Traitors and apostates are among the most virulent enemies, and those whom we have especially favored, and treated with confidence, may become our bitterest foes.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:13
segments: No one, however exalted or meritorious, can safely depend on popular favor.  At one time the people may eulogize, and at another curse him; at one time cry, Hosanna, and at another crucify him.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:19
segments:
Ittai; the commander of the Gittites. 
 
  The king; Absalom, who had proclaimed himself king. 
 
  Thou art a stranger; the Gittites were from the Philistines, but had become attached to David and his cause. 
 
A generous and benevolent mind will not wish its friends to be involved in its troubles, but will desire, as far as may be consistent, to relieve them, and to promote their enjoyment.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:21
segments: True love is gratified not only in labors, but in self-denials and sacrifices to relieve the distresses and advance the happiness of the object beloved.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:23
segments: The brook Kidron; on the east side of Jerusalem, between the city and the mount of Olives.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:24
segments: Abiathar; he was high-priest at that time.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:25
segments: Humble and hearty submission in distress to the chastising hand of God, and cheerful commitment of one's interests to him, form a good preparation for deliverance.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:27
segments: A seer; a prophet, or a wise and discerning man.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:30
segments: His head covered; in token of deep humiliation and distress.  He was reaping the fruit of kissing Absalom when he should have punished him, and also the fruit of his own sins in the matter of Uriah.
Parents for their sins are often chastised by the sins of children, which are the occasion to them and their friends of many tears.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:31
segments:
Turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness; by preventing it from helping Absalom or injuring David. 
 
A very short but hearty supplication to God may be answered in great and lasting blessings.

entries.title: II Samuel 15:36
segments: Prayer, though effcacious, does not lessen the necessity of using means; and in cases of difficulty, the more knowledge a person has with regard to them, the more properly he will be able to treat them.  But no means should be used to gain knowledge, or accomplish any object, but such as are right, and no declarations made except those which are true.
